abstract: Ornamentation, the sculpture of the outer pollen wall, is one of the central traits of pollen. However, it is mostly described with qualitative categories that rely on subjective judgment, and continuous, interpretable descriptors are still lacking. Here we used persistent homology, a fundamental method in topological data analysis, to define three interpretable descriptors (intensity, density and polarity) for three-dimensional pollen data. These descriptors form the three axes of a quantitative morphospace of pollen ornamentation, in which real, theoretical and ancestral pollen can be placed. The three axes were largely independent and separated common ornamentation types. In tests against known values, the morphospace recovered the number of ornamental elements in both theoretical pollen and real echinate pollen. Applied to pollination, it showed that, after phylogenetic correction, insect-pollinated pollen differed significantly from wind-pollinated pollen only in having more pronounced relief. In an evolutionary analysis within Asteraceae, it traced the three subfamilies diverging in different directions from their estimated common ancestor. By replacing qualitative categories with continuous, interpretable descriptors, this morphospace provides a common quantitative framework for pollen ornamentation. As three-dimensional pollen data accumulate, new grains can be placed in this morphospace without redefining the axes.
